name: Prepare and audit annual financial statements
summary: Each year the finance division prepares audited financial statements for the organisation itself and for each of its investment pools. The work starts in the autumn when the external auditor's plan is agreed and controls are tested, then after 31 December the accountants draft the statements from the closed books, supply schedules and answer the auditor's questions, while valuations defends private and fund values. The CFO signs the representation letter, the Finance and Audit Committee and Board approve, and the auditor signs the same day. Most elapsed time is waiting for year end, the December close, the auditor's fieldwork slot and committee meetings; the corporate statements are approved in late February and the pool statements later.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion that reports under IFRS, is audited by a national firm, and in 2021 ran four investment pools.
baseline.notes: Statements built in spreadsheets from the ERP and the custodian's records, with an auditor's document portal and a board portal; no disclosure management software.

unit_of_work: one set of audited annual statements
trigger: The autumn audit planning meeting opens the year-end cycle; the year-end work starts when fund accounting and the corporate ledger release the December close.
end_state: The statements are approved, the auditor's report is signed and the final statements are issued to clients, the annual report, tax and the members' meeting.

volume.seasonality: All sets run on the December year end: planning in October and November, fieldwork in January to March, approval from late February to March.

evidence.note: Organisation file: The model manager plus four pools in 2021 gives five sets a year; the infrastructure pool added a sixth from 2022.

steps.name: Agree the audit plan, timetable and request list with the auditor
steps.description: In the autumn the manager of financial reporting meets the external audit team to agree the year-end timetable for the model manager and each pool, the list of schedules and documents the model manager will provide, materiality, new accounting matters and which controls and service organisation reports the auditor will rely on.
outputs: agreed audit plan and request list

evidence.note: The auditor communicates planned scope and timing to those charged with governance; per-set time is a fifth of the joint planning effort.

steps.name: Finance and Audit Committee reviews the audit plan
steps.description: The CFO brings the auditor's plan, fees and independence confirmation to the next Finance and Audit Committee meeting, where the committee approves the plan and meets the auditor without management present.

control.basis: Finance and Audit Committee mandate (oversight of the external auditor) and auditing standards on communication with those charged with governance

evidence.note: The committee met six times in 2021, so the wait to the next meeting is up to about two months.

steps.name: Support the auditor's interim controls testing
steps.description: During the auditor's interim visit the corporate accountant arranges walkthroughs, pulls samples of journals, payments, access reviews and reconciliations, and provides the model manager's and the custodian's SOC 1 reports with bridge letters.

evidence.note: User auditors rely on SOC 1 reports; the model manager issued its first SOC 1 report in 2021.

steps.name: Wait for year end
steps.description: Nothing more can be done on the year-end balances until 31 December passes; meanwhile the team works on the monthly closes, the budget and accounting policy papers.

evidence.note: Planning in October or early November leaves about six to nine weeks to year end.

steps.name: Receive the December close and open the statements file
steps.description: Once fund accounting releases the December month-end package for the pools and the corporate ledger is closed, the manager rolls forward last year's statement templates, links the trial balances and assigns drafting work.

evidence.note: The month-end package takes about two weeks in this organisation's fund accounting close; four of five sets are pools.

steps.name: Draft the pool financial statements and notes
steps.description: A senior accountant in investment accounting prepares the pool's statements of financial position, comprehensive income and changes in net assets, the schedule of investments, the fair value hierarchy, financial risk notes and unitholder transactions from the custodian's records and the book of record.

error.defect_description: A note disagrees with the statements, or holdings are classified at the wrong fair value level.

next.condition: pool holds funds or private assets needing valuation support

evidence.note: A peer's pooled fund statements show the same components; drafting effort is an author estimate.

steps.name: Draft the model manager's corporate financial statements and notes
steps.description: The corporate accountant prepares the model manager's own statements: cost recoveries from clients, compensation and incentive accruals, leases, capital assets, pension, commitments and the agency fees administered for clients as related party transactions.

error.defect_description: Accrual or related party disclosure inconsistent with the ledger.

evidence.note: The model manager's statements contain these notes; effort is an author estimate.

steps.name: Obtain year-end valuations and fair value support
steps.description: For pools holding hedge funds or private assets, the valuations manager supplies the approved year-end values, the valuation methods and inputs, and the Level 3 roll-forward and sensitivity tables needed for the notes.
outputs: fair value support and Level 3 tables

error.defect_description: Level 3 table does not agree to the approved values.

evidence.note: Investors must evidence fund valuations with a management valuation process; waiting for fourth-quarter approvals is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare lead schedules and the auditor's request list items
steps.description: The corporate accountant assembles lead schedules tied to the trial balance, reconciliations, custodian and bank statements, agreements and policies on the request list, and uploads them to the auditor's portal.

error.defect_description: Schedule does not tie to the trial balance.

evidence.note: Request lists are standard audit practice; effort per set is an author estimate.

steps.name: External auditor performs year-end fieldwork
steps.description: The audit team confirms holdings and cash with the custodian and banks, tests valuations and income, examines unitholder or cost recovery balances and reads the draft statements, fitting the work around its other December year-end clients.

evidence.note: Confirmation and valuation testing are described; fieldwork duration and scheduling are author estimates.

steps.name: Answer auditor queries on investments and pool balances
steps.description: A senior accountant in investment accounting answers the auditor's questions on positions, prices, income, unitholder transactions and fees, pulls custodian evidence and explains reconciling items.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Answer auditor queries on corporate balances and disclosures
steps.description: The corporate accountant handles the remaining queries on accruals, cost recoveries, leases and disclosures, tracks open items on the auditor's list and chases colleagues for documents.

next.condition: auditor challenges private or fund valuations

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Respond to the auditor's challenge of valuations
steps.description: The valuations manager explains methods and inputs for the selected holdings, provides general partner audited statements and back-testing of prior estimates against later reported values, and agrees any adjustment.

evidence.note: Auditors compare valuations with other evidence and later results; share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Agree audit adjustments and disclosure changes
steps.description: The manager reviews the auditor's list of proposed adjustments and disclosure points with the corporate accountant, decides which to book and which to leave as unadjusted differences below materiality, and records the reasons.

next.condition: adjustments or disclosure changes to make

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the share of sets with changes.

steps.name: Book adjustments and revise the draft statements
steps.description: The corporate accountant posts agreed adjustments, updates the statements and notes, re-ties every number to the trial balance and sends the revised draft back to the auditor.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Manager reviews the statements and disclosure checklist
steps.description: The manager of financial reporting reads the full statements, checks the casting and cross-referencing, completes the IFRS disclosure checklist and compares the year with the prior year and the year-end close.

control.basis: Financial reporting procedure: independent review and IFRS disclosure checklist before statements go to the CFO

evidence.note: Statements are prepared under IFRS; review steps are an author estimate.

steps.name: Director of investment accounting reviews the pool statements
steps.description: The director reviews the pool statements against the closed books, the fair value levels and the risk notes, and signs off that they agree with the pool's records.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: CFO reviews and signs the management representation letter
steps.description: The chief financial officer reviews the statements and the auditor's draft findings and, with the chief executive, signs the representation letter confirming management's responsibility and the completeness of information given.

control.basis: Canadian auditing standards: written representations from management are required before the auditor's report is dated

evidence.note: The auditor's report states management's responsibility for the statements; the representation letter is standard practice.

steps.name: Prepare the Finance and Audit Committee package
steps.description: The manager assembles the statements, a summary of results and judgments, the auditor's findings report and the management letter responses, and loads them to the board portal a week before the meeting.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the Finance and Audit Committee meeting
steps.description: The package waits for the scheduled committee meeting, set months ahead to meet the reporting deadline; the corporate statements then also need the Board.

evidence.note: Six committee and ten Board meetings in 2021; the wait distribution is an author estimate.

steps.name: Committee and Board approve the statements
steps.description: The CFO presents the statements; the committee questions management and the auditor and recommends them, and the Board approves the model manager's corporate statements, which the Board chair and committee chair sign on its behalf.

control.basis: The model manager Act ss. 22 and 23 and the by-laws: audited annual statements approved by the Board (approval cannot be delegated) and delivered to the Minister within 120 days

evidence.note: Board approval of the statements is non-delegable and the 120-day deadline is stated in the OSC order.

steps.name: Auditor dates and signs the opinion
steps.description: Once approval is given and subsequent events are updated to that date, the audit partner releases the signed auditor's report, usually the same day.

evidence.note: In 2020, 2021 and 2022 the auditor's report and the Board's authorisation carry the same date.

steps.name: Issue the final statements
steps.description: The manager sends the signed statements to clients for their own audits, to communications for the annual report, to tax for the pool trust returns and to the members' meeting file, and archives the final version.

evidence.note: Audited statements go into the annual report to the Minister and to the members' meeting.

exceptions.name: Valuation support for fund or private holdings
exceptions.description: A pool holding hedge funds or private assets needs year-end valuations and Level 3 tables from the valuations team.

exceptions.name: Auditor challenges valuations
exceptions.description: The auditor selects holdings for deeper testing and the valuations manager must defend or adjust them.

exceptions.name: Audit adjustments or disclosure changes
exceptions.description: The auditor proposes adjustments or note changes that are booked and the draft revised.

exceptions.name: Reviewer or approver asks for changes
exceptions.description: The manager, director, CFO or committee sends the draft back for correction.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the autumn audit planning meeting to issue of the signed statements
benchmarks.population: Five annual statement sets (corporate and pools) of a Canadian public-sector asset manager, 2019 to 2022

evidence.note: Derived: planning about 60 to 75 days before year end; the model manager's corporate statements were authorised 55 to 61 days after year end and a peer's pooled fund statements 101 days after; the model manager's pool statements are assumed to fall between, about 70 to 90 days.

benchmarks.population: The model manager corporate financial statements

evidence.note: Authorised 25 February 2021, 24 February 2022 and 2 March 2023.

benchmarks.population: BCI public equity pooled funds, December 2021

evidence.note: Authorised 11 April 2022.
The model manager Act s.23 as summarised in the OSC order.

pain_points.description: Year-end work cannot start until the December close is released, and the auditor's fieldwork slot is fixed around its other December clients, so a few weeks of waiting sit in the middle of a tight timetable.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on the close and audit timings.

pain_points.description: Private and fund valuations are the main audit judgment; support must be assembled from general partner reports that arrive late and the auditor may challenge them.

evidence.note: GP confirmations alone are not adequate evidence; roll-forward and valuation testing are needed.

pain_points.description: Statements, notes and lead schedules are built in spreadsheets and re-tied by hand after each adjustment, so revisions consume review time.

evidence.note: Common practice in the reference period.

pain_points.description: Committee meetings are fixed months ahead, so a late query or change pushes approval to a special meeting or close to the statutory deadline.

evidence.note: Six committee meetings a year and a 120-day statutory deadline.

sources.title: Public Equity Pooled Fund Financial Statements, December 2021

sources.supports: A general partner's confirmation alone is not adequate audit evidence for valuation; higher quality evidence includes audited fund statements, a comprehensive management valuation process and investment-level confirmation; roll-forward of fund valuations and discussion with auditors about valuation testing.

assumptions: One case is one set of statements: The model manager's corporate statements (one in five cases) or one pool's statements (four in five). Planning, interim testing and lead schedule work shared by all sets are shown at a share of their total time per case.

The organisation file lists the external auditor's audit opinion as a trigger. The opinion is the result of this process, so it is placed in interfaces.inputs as the prior year's opinion and management letter carried into planning, and the case is started by the year-end cycle and the December close package.

The OSC order exempts the model manager's pools from the securities-law financial statement requirements (NI 81-106 Part 2), so audited pool statements are assumed to be required by the pool documents and by clients' own auditors rather than by securities law; the organisation file's assumption of four pool sets is kept.

The case starts at the autumn planning meeting, so the cycle time includes waiting for year end; measured from year end, the simulated median is about 60 days, a little longer than the model manager's 55 to 61 days for its corporate statements and shorter than the 101 days of the peer's pooled funds.

Pool statements are approved by the Finance and Audit Committee and the corporate statements also by the Board; the exact approval body for pool statements is not public (a peer's pooled fund statements are authorised by its CEO/CIO).
Hands-on time of about 90 hours of the model manager staff time per set is the author's estimate; auditor hours are outside the organisation and shown as external waits.
Web search capacity ran out while researching this file, so auditing standard texts were not opened; rules named in controls come from the model manager's own reports and the OSC order.
Loaded costs per hour are taken unchanged from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading).
